text: Taste, sometimes I think we think of as this inaccessible thing that, "Oh, that person was born with taste." I see it as a skill that it can develop. I think is extremely important to try lots of products.
speaker: Guillermo Rauch
context: Lenny asks Guillermo about building taste, a quality people often struggle to develop when creating products. Guillermo explains that taste isn't an innate gift but rather a developable skill. He shares Vercel's internal principle of "increasing exposure hours" - deliberately spending time observing how people interact with products to build better product intuition.
text_ko: 취향(taste)은 가끔 우리가 '아, 저 사람은 타고난 감각이야'라며 도달할 수 없는 무언가로 여기는 것 같아요. 저는 오히려 취향을 개발할 수 있는 기술이라고 생각해요. 여러 제품을 많이 써보는 게 정말 중요해요.
text_zh: 品味这个东西，我觉得大家有时候会误以为是天生的，觉得"哎呀，那个人天生就有品味"。但我觉得品味其实是一种技能，是可以培养的。所以我认为多去体验各种产品是非常重要的。
text_es: El buen gusto, a veces creo que lo vemos como algo inalcanzable, como "ay, esa persona nació con buen gusto." Yo lo veo como una habilidad que se puede desarrollar. Creo que es súper importante probar muchos productos.
key_sentence: Taste is a skill that can develop through exposure hours.
original_text: Taste, sometimes I think we think of as this inaccessible thing that, "Oh, that person was born with taste." I see it as a skill that it can develop. I think is extremely important to try lots of products. We have one of our internal operating principles as increasing exposure hours. Try to quantify how much time you expose yourself to watching how people use your products and you'll develop that muscle.

vocabulary.definition: Not able to be reached, entered, or obtained; difficult to access or understand.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'inaccessible' can refer to markets, resources, or information that are difficult for a company to reach or utilize, potentially limiting growth opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used to describe physical barriers, it can also imply a lack of understanding or availability in a metaphorical sense.

vocabulary.definition: To grow or cause to grow and become more mature, advanced, or elaborate.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'develop' often refers to the process of creating new products, services, or strategies to enhance competitiveness and meet market demands.
vocabulary.nuance: This term suggests a gradual process of improvement and innovation rather than immediate change.

vocabulary.definition: Of the highest significance or value; crucial for success or effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, labeling something as 'extremely important' emphasizes its critical role in decision-making, strategy formulation, or operational success.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase conveys urgency and priority, suggesting that neglecting the matter could lead to significant consequences.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to do something well, usually gained through training or experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, 'skill' refers to the competencies that employees possess, which are essential for performing tasks effectively and contributing to organizational success.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with technical abilities, 'skill' can also encompass soft skills such as communication and teamwork.

text: A lot of the programming jobs to be done that used to be specializations, I think, are going away, in a way.
speaker: Guillermo Rauch
context: Lenny asks about the future of engineering careers and whether people should still learn to code. Guillermo explains that many programming tasks are essentially translation jobs (like converting designs to code) that AI can now handle. However, he emphasizes that understanding the underlying systems and technologies remains crucial because this knowledge helps you communicate more effectively with AI models.
text_ko: 한때 전문화돼 있던 많은 프로그래밍 업무들이 어떤 면에서는 사라지고 있는 것 같아요.
text_zh: 以前那些需要专门技能的编程工作，我觉得很多都在慢慢消失。
text_es: Muchos de los trabajos de programación que antes eran especializaciones, creo que están desapareciendo, de alguna manera.
key_sentence: A lot of the programming jobs to be done that used to be specializations, I think, are going away, in a way.
original_text: A lot of the programming jobs to be done that used to be specializations, I think, are going away, in a way. They're translation tasks, but knowing how things work under the hood is going to be very important for you because you're going to be able to influence the model and make it follow your intention a lot better.

vocabulary.definition: Specializations refer to specific areas of expertise or focused skill sets within a broader field. They allow individuals or organizations to concentrate their efforts on particular tasks or industries.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, specializations can determine the division of labor, with professionals focusing on niche areas to enhance efficiency and innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'specializations' implies a depth of knowledge, it can also suggest a limitation in versatility; it is often used when discussing roles that require deep expertise.

vocabulary.definition: Programming is the process of designing and building executable computer software to accomplish a specific task. It involves writing code in various programming languages.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, programming is essential for developing software products, automating processes, and enhancing user experiences, making it a core competency for tech teams.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'programming' can imply both the technical aspects of coding and the strategic planning involved in software development; it is often used in discussions about software engineering and product development.

text: People could be more full stack. Imagine a designer that can ship a fully baked product, a product manager that can prototype and ship to production.
speaker: Guillermo Rauch
context: Lenny asks how AI tools like v0 will change product development for product managers and teams. Guillermo envisions a future where traditional role boundaries blur, enabled by AI tools that make it easier to build and ship products. He believes people will become more versatile, with designers able to create complete products and product managers able to build working prototypes.
text_ko: 사람들이 더 풀스택(full stack)이 될 수 있어요. 예를 들어 완성된 제품을 통째로 출시할 수 있는 디자이너나, 프로토타입(prototype)을 직접 만들어 프로덕션(production)까지 배포할 수 있는 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)를 상상해 보세요.
text_zh: 其实大家都可以更全能一些。你想想，如果设计师能直接做出完整的产品，产品经理能自己做原型还能直接上线，那该多厉害。
text_es: La gente podría ser más integral. Imagínate un diseñador que pueda lanzar un producto completamente terminado, o un product manager que pueda hacer prototipos y llevarlo hasta producción.
key_sentence: Imagine a designer that can ship a fully baked product, a product manager that can prototype and ship to production.
original_text: People could be more full stack. Imagine a designer that can ship a fully baked product, a product manager that can prototype and ship to production. We shouldn't put limits on ourselves and what we can build, and what we can ship, and what we can dream about making possible on these web surfaces.

vocabulary.definition: A term used to describe a professional who is proficient in both front-end and back-end development, encompassing all layers of software development.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, a full stack developer can handle the entire development process, making them highly valuable for small teams that require versatility and efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'full stack' typically refers to software development, it can also imply a broader skill set in other fields, such as design or product management.

vocabulary.definition: An early sample or model of a product used to test and validate concepts before full-scale production.
vocabulary.businessContext: Prototyping is crucial in product development as it allows teams to gather feedback and make iterative improvements before launching a final product.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a rough draft or a more polished version, depending on the context of the development phase.

vocabulary.definition: The process of deploying a completed product or feature to a live environment where it is accessible to end users.
vocabulary.businessContext: In software development, 'shipping to production' signifies the transition from development to operational status, marking a critical milestone in the product lifecycle.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the readiness and quality of the product, suggesting that it has passed all necessary testing and is suitable for public use.

text: One of the bets that I made early on with Vercel that really paid off is Vercel, maybe as a metaphor is like AWS in easy mode for a lot of people.
speaker: Guillermo Rauch
context: Guillermo explains Vercel's positioning in the market and how they've made complex cloud infrastructure accessible to more developers. He describes how Vercel simplifies cloud deployment compared to AWS, allowing developers to reach massive scale without needing deep infrastructure knowledge, citing the example of a customer handling 43X traffic increases seamlessly.
text_ko: 제가 초기에 Vercel에 건 한 베팅이 정말 잘 맞았어요. Vercel은 많은 사람들한테 AWS(아마존 웹 서비스)를 ‘쉬운 모드’로 만들어 준 것 같아요.
text_zh: 我在Vercel早期下的一个赌注真的很成功，可以这么说，Vercel对很多人来说就像是简化版的AWS。
text_es: Una de las apuestas que hice desde el principio con Vercel que realmente dio resultado es que Vercel, como metáfora, es como AWS pero en modo fácil para mucha gente.
key_sentence: Vercel is like AWS in easy mode for those needing cloud flexibility.
original_text: One of the bets that I made early on with Vercel that really paid off is Vercel, maybe as a metaphor is like AWS in easy mode for a lot of people. We have a very large user base of people that would have otherwise not have been able to configure all of the ins and outs of the cloud, but do want the scale, flexibility, speed, et cetera.

vocabulary.definition: A figure of speech that describes an object or action in a way that isn't literally true but helps explain an idea or make a comparison.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, metaphors are often used in marketing and branding to create relatable imagery that resonates with customers, making complex concepts more understandable.
vocabulary.nuance: While metaphors can enhance communication, they should be used carefully to avoid confusion or misinterpretation.

text: The secrets of product quality is blood, sweat, and tears. The other thing is that a great product is made up of a thousand little details and so you're never really done.
speaker: Guillermo Rauch
context: Lenny references Guillermo's tweet about product quality requiring "blood, sweat, and tears" and asks him to elaborate. Guillermo explains that building great products requires intense attention to countless small details and involves difficult trade-offs. He uses the metaphor of adopting a puppy to describe how each new feature requires ongoing care and maintenance, which is why successful product builders must be highly selective.
text_ko: 제품 품질(product quality)의 비결은 피와 땀, 눈물이에요. 또 훌륭한 제품은 수많은 작은 디테일들로 이루어져 있어서 진짜로 끝나는 일이 없어요.
text_zh: 产品质量的秘诀就是要付出血汗，拼命去做。还有就是，一个好产品是由无数个小细节组成的，所以你永远都做不完，得一直优化下去。
text_es: La clave de la calidad de un producto está en dejarse la piel trabajando. Y además, un gran producto se construye con mil pequeños detalles, así que nunca terminas realmente.
key_sentence: a great product is made up of a thousand little details and so you're never really done.
original_text: The secrets of product quality is blood, sweat, and tears. The other thing is that a great product is made up of a thousand little details and so you're never really done. There's a humility that comes from the process also of why the best product builders will say nine nos for every yes. Because when you say yes, it's like adopting a puppy.

vocabulary.definition: The measure of a product's ability to meet customer expectations and requirements, often assessed through durability, reliability, and performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, maintaining high product quality is essential for customer satisfaction and brand reputation, influencing repeat purchases and market competitiveness.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'product quality' encompasses both tangible and intangible aspects, and it is important to specify the criteria being evaluated to avoid ambiguity.

text: I foresee a lot of people becoming incredibly impactful in building and shipping amazing products, and building gigantic companies, and everything you could imagine, where a single person can do the job of a hundred different people in a hundred different specializations.
speaker: Guillermo Rauch
context: Lenny asks about the future of engineering careers and whether people should still learn to code. Guillermo envisions a future where AI tools will dramatically amplify individual productivity, allowing one person to accomplish work that previously required large teams with diverse specializations. He sees this as democratizing the ability to build successful products and companies.
text_ko: 앞으로 많은 사람들이 멋진 제품을 만들고 출시하면서 거대한 회사를 세우고 상상할 수 있는 거의 모든 일을 해내며 엄청난 영향력을 발휘할 것 같아요. 한 사람이 백 명의 서로 다른 전문 분야에서 하던 일을 해낼 수 있는 시대가 올 거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得以后会有很多人变得超级厉害，能做出特别棒的产品，建立巨无霸公司，你能想到的各种事情他们都能做到，一个人就能顶一百个不同专业领域的人。
text_es: Veo que mucha gente va a lograr un impacto increíble creando y lanzando productos espectaculares, construyendo empresas enormes, y todo lo que te puedas imaginar, donde una sola persona va a poder hacer el trabajo de cien personas diferentes en cien especializaciones distintas.
key_sentence: A single person can be incredibly impactful in building gigantic companies.

vocabulary.definition: Having a significant effect or influence on a situation or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being impactful often refers to the ability of a product, strategy, or individual to create substantial change or drive results within an organization or market.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'impactful' conveys a strong positive effect, it can sometimes imply a lack of subtlety or nuance in the approach taken.

vocabulary.definition: The process of focusing on a particular area of expertise or skill within a broader field.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, specializations allow individuals and teams to develop deep knowledge and skills that contribute to the overall success of projects or products.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a depth of knowledge in a specific area, which can be advantageous, but may also imply a lack of versatility.
